title: Multi-Mode Receiver and Crown Aerial Installation for Authorisation Required Approaches

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Introduction of a satellite-based augmentation capable multi-mode receiver together with a repositioned upper fuselage aerial, giving the aircraft the lateral and vertical performance required for authorisation required approaches.

sections.reason: Operators flying into terrain-constrained airports asked for authorisation required approach capability, which the previous receiver could not support because its vertical protection level is computed from an older augmentation standard. Independently, the aerial fitted at build sits far enough aft on the crown to be shadowed by the vertical stabilizer at high bank angles, which was showing up as brief loss of satellite geometry in the turn. Both items had to be resolved together because approving the approach capability requires a substantiated aerial position as well as a receiver standard.
sections.description: The multi-mode receiver interface unit D3450112668148 and the upper receiver computer sub-assembly D3450113750314 are replaced by units of the new standard, and the forward circuit card QUD432161-77 is superseded by a card carrying the augmentation processing. The dependent position determining transceiver D3450007115686 is retained but is moved 1 400 mm forward on the crown, to a reinforced pad between frames 44 and 48, so that the vertical stabilizer no longer shadows it above 25 degrees of bank. The parameter database LH4L19EEBC2 is loaded to the new receiver standard through the normal data loading interface. Coaxial runs are re-made to the new aerial position and are routed along the existing crown cable route. Work is in the ceiling void, zone 293, and in the avionics bay, zone 162, with the crown skin pad installed from outside. Detail is on drawing D34501177112.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 2.7 kg per aircraft, forward of the reference datum, with no reportable balance effect. Electrical load is unchanged; the new receiver draws the same 140 VA as the unit it replaces. The receiver is one-way interchangeable with the previous standard provided the aerial has already been moved, and not interchangeable at all if it has not, which is the reason the two are released as a single modification. The aircraft flight manual gains the authorisation required approach capability. The navigation database loading procedure is unchanged. Wiring content for the crown route requires update, and the avionics bay equipment list changes.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN S01593 in May 2021 across the twin-engine range. Retrofit is through Service Bulletin SLN-34-1041, which includes the crown pad installation and therefore needs the aircraft in a hangar; typical embodiment is four days. The aerial pad is the long-lead item at twenty-two weeks.

type_data.balance_impact: Forward of the reference datum; no reportable shift
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN S01593; crown pad added to the Section 15 build
